text:
Sam Cheng: Quick RFC follow-up — we need to decide intent-vs-enforcement semantics for model binding metadata. I sketched a compact schema and migration plan below. Thoughts? :thinking:

Sam Cheng: Proposed metadata (YAML for readability):
```yaml
model_id: 'gptx-13b'
model_version: 'v2026-03-01'
pin_intent:
  owner: 'feature/semantic-rerank'
  since: 1749980000
  reason: 'safety/regression testing'
  expiry_intent: 1749999000   # optional, a soft intention from owner
enforcement:
  lease_until: 1750002000   # optional, server-enforced expiry (absolute ts)
  enforced_by: 'allocation-service'
  fallback_model: 'gptx-7b-quant'
hints: [ 'low-latency-variant', 'quantized-4bit' ]
opaque_tags: [ 'canary-042' ]
```

Sam Cheng: Tradeoffs I see: 1) intent-only (sticky annotations) is simple for client semantics but leaves stale pins. 2) server-enforced leases avoid resource leaks but add leader/clock complexity and renew/rollback logic.

Anya Patel: +1 to keeping both. Intent expresses business need; lease encodes operational guardrails. Recommend precedence: enforcement lease wins if present. Clients should be informed via headers. :+1:

Jordan Lee: Concern: how do we handle clock skew across regions? If lease_until is slightly in the past on one host it might immediately evict. We need a grace window or vector-clock style checks.

Lina Morales: Agreed. Suggest two small rules: enforce only after lease_until + 30s grace, and require verification with placement leader before hard evict. Also make lease renewals idempotent with CAS token.

Mike O'Rourke: DB migration notes: `model_pins` currently has columns (model_id, tenant_id, pinned_at). We'll add: intent_json TEXT, lease_until BIGINT NULL, enforced_by TEXT NULL, fallback_model_id TEXT NULL. Add index on (tenant_id, lease_until) for cleanup. Example SQL: 
```sql
ALTER TABLE model_pins ADD COLUMN intent_json TEXT;
ALTER TABLE model_pins ADD COLUMN lease_until BIGINT;
ALTER TABLE model_pins ADD COLUMN enforced_by TEXT;
ALTER TABLE model_pins ADD COLUMN fallback_model_id TEXT;
CREATE INDEX idx_pins_tenant_lease ON model_pins(tenant_id, lease_until);
```

Mike O'Rourke: Plan: write migration that backfills intent_json from existing comments, run for 48h, enable writes to both schema shapes during backfill.

Anya Patel: API semantics proposal: GET /resolve -> returns resolved model and headers: X-Model-Pin-Intent, X-Model-Pin-Lease (ts), X-Model-Pin-Source (owner|enforcer). Clients that see lease expiring should prefetch fallback. Example curl: 
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/resolve?tenant=acme" -I
# -> X-Model-Pin-Lease: 1750002000
```

Jordan Lee: Edge-case: what if enforcement agent fails mid-evict? Need safe rollback. Suggest moves are two-phase: mark -> drain -> evict. Mark uses CAS token stored in model_pins.intent_json or separate column so other agents won't race.

Lina Morales: Observability: emit metrics for pin_create, pin_renewal, pin_eviction, eviction_failures, and attach trace_id to each enforcement op. Also log reason and owner. Add an eval check that flags sudden fallback swaps in production traffic.

ops-bot: Note: scheduled job `pin-lease-cleaner` will run every 60s. It respects lease_until + 30s grace and leader election. Running in dry-run for 6 hours in prod namespace.

Sam Cheng: Proposal for precedence & migration summary: 1) If enforcement.lease_until exists and now > lease_until + grace -> enforcement takes effect. 2) Else use pin_intent as advisory only. 3) During migration support both fields; deprecate intent-only after 3 months.

Anya Patel: Approves plan. Can we add a small client library helper that reads headers and retries against fallback automatically? DevEx can ship in next SDK patch.

Sam Cheng: Agreed — Lina/Jordan/Mike, can you file follow-up tasks? I'll open RFC patch with the schema and the migration plan. Thanks all. :rocket:
